headline: Democrats take Congress as oil retreats on Iran peace hopes
summary: The U.S. midterms handed Democrats both chambers, and by week's end the House had shelved a Republican's bid to impeach Pete Hegseth while hopes for an end to the Iran war pushed Brent crude below US$90. In Canada, the Carney government's budget set a $62.3-billion deficit, and in Ontario the province appointed powerful regional chairs as Toronto froze hiring over a $1.1-billion gap.

top.headline: Democrats flip Congress; two Senate races still being counted
top.what: Democrats are projected to hold at least 259 House seats and at least 54 Senate seats, with Democratic challengers leading by about 2,500 votes in still-uncalled Alaska and Mississippi.
top.why: Control of Congress shifts in January, opening the way to challenges on tariffs and Trump's agenda.

top.headline: Oil falls below US$90 as Trump signals Iran war could end
top.what: After limited U.S. strikes and a disabled cargo ship early in the week, Trump met Qatar's prime minister and said new strikes are unlikely; Brent dropped about 25% from its October peak, though Iran denies talks.
top.why: Oil prices drive Canadian inflation, gas prices and the Bank of Canada's rate path.

top.headline: Carney's second budget: $62.3B deficit, $142B in new spending
top.what: The federal budget projects a $62.3-billion deficit for 2026-27 and adds about $142 billion in new spending over five years, including a 10-year plan to end homelessness and a $2 stamp in 2027.
top.why: It sets federal taxes, transfers and borrowing for years to come.

top.headline: House shelves Hegseth impeachment, 211-204
top.what: Rep. Thomas Massie forced a vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, but the House voted 211-204 on Nov. 10 to send it to committee, ending it in this Congress.
top.why: Democrats can revive the fight over the Iran war once they control the House in January.

top.headline: Ford appoints eight 'strong' regional chairs, including Del Duca in York
top.what: Ontario named appointed chairs for Durham, Halton, Muskoka, Niagara, Peel, Waterloo and York, plus the Simcoe warden, with powers over staff, bylaws and budgets.
top.why: Regional chairs now shape GTA property-tax budgets and housing approvals.

top.headline: Toronto freezes hiring after Ford rules out a new funding deal
top.what: Facing a $1.1-billion 2027 shortfall, Toronto paused most hiring after the premier said the province will not sign a second 'New Deal'.
top.why: It points to tax, fare or service pressure in the next city budget.

top.headline: Republicans pick Jordan for House, keep Thune in Senate
top.what: House Republicans elected Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise as minority leader, and Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune after a failed push to delay.
top.why: These leaders will steer the GOP response to a Democratic Congress.

top.headline: Ontario students walk out over OSAP as career-college aid stays frozen
top.what: Thousands of students protested OSAP changes and tuition on Nov. 5; Ford dismissed the protests Tuesday while aid to private career colleges remains frozen pending audits.
top.why: Student aid decides what post-secondary education costs GTA families.
